title: SUIT · cerebellar lobules and deep nuclei
units_evidence: The publisher SUIT template descriptor gives a 1 mm grid; T1 and probability NIfTI headers declare millimeters. The categorical image shares the probability affine and sample grid.

space.name: Original SUIT cerebellar population template
space.reference: DiedrichsenLab cerebellar_atlases at 6857dfa732de6dd60c94da2f84d0b15ccf316618; tpl-SUIT descriptors and original NIfTI affines.
space.correspondence: The publisher provides the T1 template, categorical atlas and probability fields in SUIT space. Labels and probabilities retain their original negative X index direction; T1 retains its positive X index direction. Physical millimeter coordinates link all views.

sources.title: SUIT anatomical cerebellar atlas and original template
sources.citation: Diedrichsen J (2006). A spatially unbiased atlas template of the human cerebellum. NeuroImage 33:127-138. Diedrichsen J et al. (2009). A probabilistic MR atlas of the human cerebellum. NeuroImage 46:39-46. Diedrichsen J et al. (2011). Imaging the deep cerebellar nuclei: A probabilistic atlas and normalization procedure. NeuroImage 54:1786-1794. Original definitions reference Schmahmann et al. (2000).
sources.license_name: Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial 3.0 Unported; specific SUIT template, associated files and atlases notice

label_table.evidence: Original source categorical assignment on the SUIT population template; source MRI-based manual delineations followed by author normalization and probability summarization.
source_notes: Lobules (1–28): 20 healthy young participants. Deep nuclei (29–34): a separate group of 23 participants, imaged with source susceptibility-weighted MRI at 7 T.
The displayed T1 is the original population template and supplies shared spatial context. Fine nuclear identity is supplied by the source atlas.
The source combines lobules I–IV and combines emboliform and globose nuclei as Interposed. Delivered grouping and sampled extent are retained.
Original categorical assignments and scaled probability samples are preserved independently. Unsmooth half-voxel categorical boundaries provide the 3D surfaces.
label_table.display_color_evidence: Teaching display palette distinguishes dentate, interposed and fastigial compartments against the dark viewer background. Original source colors, numeric assignments and geometry are retained in the provenance.

probability_interpretation: Source population assignment fractions for each compartment after author normalization into SUIT space. Lobular and nuclear fields describe separate participant groups.
probability_derivation: Extract each original 4D frame exactly with its native affine and header scaling. Explicit channel-to-label binding follows the publisher numeric ordering and is checked against all categorical voxels: the associated channel attains the maximum at every assigned voxel, allowing an original quantization tie.
probability_rounding_evidence: The original uint8 probability NIfTI uses float32 slope 0.003921568859368563 and zero intercept. The scaled value for 255 is 1.0000000591389835. Values are retained exactly; tolerance covers this recorded encoding precision only.
acquisition: Run neuroimage acquire suit_cerebellum --data-root <existing-data-root>. Pinned original files are reused by SHA256; each image remains in its delivered native array and space.

teaching_sequences.title: Hemispheric lobules
teaching_sequences.objective: Identify the source-defined hemispheric lobules in the original SUIT template.
teaching_sequences.instruction: Follow the selected assignment through three original MRI planes, compare source probability support and rotate the complete displayed 3D compartments.
teaching_sequences.evidence_limit: Coverage: original 1 mm SUIT population template and source MRI-derived assignments. Source cohort, categorical boundaries and continuous support are recorded separately.
teaching_sequences.step_prompt: Describe the selected compartment and its position relative to the other displayed source regions.
teaching_sequences.step_question: Which compartment is selected, which neighboring assignments are visible, and how does its source probability vary across adjacent MRI samples?
